name: The Shift — UBE University Demo
tagline: Gamified bar prep for law schools — full exam-day simulation without another dry LMS.
audience: Law school deans · clinical professors · academic technology · bar prep partnerships
estimatedSecNote: Actual duration is driven by ElevenLabs per-line synthesis in DemoForge
presenterNotes: Frame: students already use Anki and games — bar prep should feel like training, not homework.
Emphasize: placeholder MBE copy is intentional; mechanics and exam-day flow are the demo.
Close: pilot with one 1L skills section — we measure engagement, not pass rates, in semester one.

steps.narration: This is The Shift configured for the Uniform Bar Exam — built for a law school pilot, not a consumer launch. Same gamification engine as our healthcare verticals, tuned for issue-spotting under pressure.
Students see a mission dashboard — bar exam countdown, rolling accuracy, and one-click deploy into the modes they'll actually use during bar season.
Exam Day is the headline for your faculty demo — a full UBE mission chain: morning MBE, lunch lockout, essays, and MPT file work. Each block routes to a working mode, not a slide deck.
The progress rail mirrors real bar day pacing. You can walk through the chain live or jump straight into any block for a deep dive.
Study Hub maps mastery across all seven MBE subjects — civil procedure through torts — so instructors can see where a cohort is weak before grades slip.
Every domain links into Category Deep Dive, timed exams, and the War Room arsenal. One vertical switch; no separate product to maintain.
War Room is where the gamification lives — Clinic Shift scenarios at the core, MBE simulations on the dial, and bar-prep modes surfaced for the UBE pack.
Faculty can queue a training plan — issue spotter, essay forge, file room, exam day — or double-tap any node to deploy solo. Students feel like they're running missions, not checking boxes.

Essay Forge is timed MEE practice — prompt on screen, countdown running, student drafts in-browser, then self-grade against a model outline. Content is placeholder today; the session mechanics are production-ready.
One click drops them into a thirty-minute essay block — the same rhythm they'll need on exam day.
File Room is the MPT — task memo, library files, and statute tabs on the left; objective memorandum editor on the right, with a grading checklist when they submit.
Split-pane layout matches how bar takers actually work — read the file, write the memo, no context switching.
Issue Spotter is the arcade layer — short fact patterns, tag every live doctrine, score streaks for correct tags minus false alarms. It trains the skill bar examiners actually test.
MBE blocks use blueprint-driven exams — quick drill, half session, or full two-hundred-question simulation with section breaks and flag-for-review, just like the real thing.
Clinic Shift is our field-work mode — client intake, ethics calls, discovery deadlines — scored like a shift simulation, not a multiple-choice quiz.
Circuit Split is the boss fight — phased MBE encounters with an HP bar. Miss a question and the boss hits back. Students remember the pain of losing a phase.

For your university meeting: every mode you saw is functional on placeholder content today. Scale the question bank with your faculty later — the engagement architecture is already here. Let's talk about a one-section pilot.
